newsitem.title: USA: LaserSight closes $8 mln credit facility.
newsitem.headline: LaserSight closes $8 mln credit facility.

text.p: LaserSight Inc said Monday it completed an $8 million credit facility with Foothill Capital Corp, a unit of Norwest Corp, on April 1.

The asset-based financing consists of a $4 million term loan with interest at 12.5 percent and a $4 million revolver at prime plus 1.5 percent. The revolver, based on eligible receivables, is currently available, the company said.

LaserSight said it granted the lender five-year warrants to purchase 500,000 shares of LaserSight common stock, or about 5.6 percent of the shares outstanding, exercisable as of March 31, 1998 at a price of $6.0667 per share.

Principal on the term loan is payable in installments between May and July 1998. The amount available under the revolver will decrease in monthly installments beginning August 1, 1998, the company said.
LaserSight said it was represented by A.G. Edwards & Sons in its discussions with Foothill.
The company said it used a portion of the term loan to pay the balance due to the former owners of MEC Health Care Inc, a wholly owned subsidiary of LaserSight acquired in October 1995.

LaserSight said it continues to explore various alternatives to enable it to fund the purchase under its previously announced agreement certain patent rights from International Business Machines Corp on or before July 1, 1997.
